text:
sanjay: quick follow-up on the slot-granule residency provenance prototype i ran this morning — short thread with results and a couple questions :eyes:

oleg: cool, lay it out. what did you measure?

sanjay: end-to-end: 24h stress run across 4 hosts, mixed tenants, sparse embedding workloads. compared current host-staging (per-page) vs new slot-granule hints (coarse per-segment hints emitted by runtime). results: median p50 token latency +3ms, p95 +8ms, but host memory churn down ~42% and vram eviction count down ~37%.

maya: nice. can you paste the config you used?

sanjay: sure — here's the minimal flag set i toggled on the runtime image:

```
--residency.provenance=slot-granule
--slot.size-b = 65536  # 64KB granule
--residency.hint-window-ms=200
--evict.threshold=0.78
```

sanjay: also we enabled conservative demote backpressure so tenant bursts don't instantly reclaim the whole working set.

harper: were these all synthetic inferences or live traffic?

sanjay: mixed. 60% synthetic spike tests to exercise eviction paths, 40% live-like replay of production traces (small batch chat + delayed long-completion requests).

kyle: where does the provenance info live? do we add meta per allocation or is it implicit via segment ownership?

oleg: good Q. implementation we used for the prototype kept a lightweight provenance tag per slot (8 bytes) indexed in a sidecar bitmap. no per-allocation linked lists. that keeps read/write cheap but increases side metadata.

maya: any regressions for small models? sounds like coarsening could hurt tiny working sets.

sanjay: yep we saw a handful of regressions on <8MB peak models — because slot granule > model hotspot. p95 worse by ~12ms there. but we can detect small-model footprints and fall back to per-page residency dynamically.

tia: how confident are you that the 8-byte tag approach is safe under GC/compaction? racey updates could corrupt provenance.

oleg: we protected writes with a compare-and-swap and make updates idempotent: tag transitions only go forward in provenance states (e.g., cold->warm->hot). compaction path clears tags for reclaimed memory. still want a formal proof though.

sanjay: noted. i also added telemetry hooks: emitted provenance histograms and a compactness ratio metric so we can alert if coarsening causes too much overlap.

infra-bot: deploy finished on canary cluster ci-23 (image: residency-proto:v2) — 2026-03-23T10:12:03Z

kyle: what's the rollback plan if we see small-model regressions at scale?

sanjay: plan A: dynamic detector — if a workload's compactness_ratio < 0.6 for 5m, switch that tenant to per-page mode. Plan B: global kill switch on config service + warm fallback model variant (less aggressive batching).

harper: tenant switching sounds hairy for mixed-tenancy nodes. how do you prevent oscillation?

sanjay: hysteresis on both dimensions — require 2 consecutive 5m windows to flip, and a cooldown of 15m before re-evaluating. also keep a leadership lease per-tenant to avoid flip-flopping across nodes.

oleg: tradeoff question: metadata overhead (sidecar bitmap) vs accuracy of provenance. we measured ~6% memory overhead in our canary due to side metadata. is that acceptable?

maya: 6% is fine if it buys 37% fewer evictions. we should model cost across rent-a-gpu prices though — show me the unit economics.

sanjay: agreed. i'll run a cost model next — linking raw numbers here later.

kyle: final thought: we should formalize the API boundary for "residency hint producers" so model compilers, request router, and batching layer can emit hints. we don't want each layer to invent one-off formats.

sanjay: yes — proposal: a tiny protobuf: {slot_index, provenance_state, source_enum, ttl_ms}. i've sketched it in a doc i'll link in the RFC follow-up.

harper: please include allowed transitions and GC semantics in that doc — ops needs exact behavior for incident runbooks.

sanjay: will do. thanks all. next steps: unit cost model, race-proof tag update audit, proto spec + RFC follow-up. cc @oleg @maya @kyle for review :thumbsup:
